app info: Translater is a desktop application for translating texts between more than 130 languages, built using PyQt6 by Ahmed Elmimouni. Translation, spelling correction and text-to-speech are powered by Google Gemini AI models (a Gemini API key is required, set it in Settings), while audio-to-text uses the SpeechRecognition library. It supports importing texts from text files, automatic clipboard pasting, saving translation results on the device, converting audio and video files of any size and almost any format into text (large files are split automatically into short parts), rendering text into images for supported languages, and converting the translation into speech with a choice of Gemini TTS model, voice and speaking style.
how to use:
How to use the program:

1) Input Text: If there is text in your clipboard, it will be automatically pasted directly into the upper text input field. You can also type manually or import a text file (.txt) via the File > Open File menu or the shortcut Ctrl+O.
2) Choose Target Language: Select the target language from the drop-down list at the top of the window. The program recognizes the source language automatically.
3) Translate: Press the Translate button or use the shortcut Ctrl+T. The 'start translate' message appears immediately and translation begins in the background. Translation is performed by the Gemini model you choose in Settings (a Gemini API key is required).
4) View Results: When translation finishes, the output text appears in the bottom field.
5) Save File: To save the result on your device, use the File > Save File menu or the shortcut Ctrl+S. The program automatically suggests a file name that includes the language name and saves it by default in the Documents/translater folder.
6) Clear Texts: Clear the input text using the shortcut Ctrl+D or via the File menu. Clear the output text using the shortcut Ctrl+Shift+D or via the File menu.
7) Audio to Text (Ctrl+2): Choose an audio or video file of any size and almost any format (mp3, m4a, wav, ogg, opus, flac, wma, amr, mp4, mkv, and more; use 'All files' for other extensions). Large files are split automatically at silences into short parts that are converted one by one with the SpeechRecognition library (you choose the language spoken in the file before conversion, and parts that are silent or recognized with low confidence are skipped), with progress announced. Press Ctrl+2 again during the process to cancel; the text transcribed so far is kept.
8) Text to Image: Render translated texts into image files for supported languages, allowing you to easily share or save your translations visually.
9) Text to Speech: After translating, open Options > Text to speech (Ctrl+4). The translation appears in a read-only box, with a list of speech models, a list of voices (focus the voices list and press Space to hear a short sample), and an optional speaking style field (for example: cheerfully, slowly, in a whisper). Press 'Convert to speech'; when it finishes, the Play, Stop and Save buttons appear.
